title: Spin up governed demo and pilot projects fast from a golden path
intent: /scaffold lets the owner spin up governed demo and pilot projects fast. It starts each project from a golden-path bundle, shaped by a short owner interview. The output stays local until the owner pushes it, and all generated data is fictional.

outcomes.title: /scaffold asks four questions, picks the typescript-nextjs bundle and generates a working local project whose CI enforces the gates.
outcomes.intent: One thin path from interview to a working project, for one stack, before any breadth.

outcomes.title: /scaffold generates python-fastapi and go-data-pipeline projects, names each gap that no bundle covers, and shares its copy script with /handover.
Generated CI checks layer boundaries and the bundle-size budget, and one file lists each gate and the spec answer that set it.
Each scaffolded project is ready to show, with a short demo script for its main happy path.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The interview asks for service shape, language, host and coverage floor through AskUserQuestion, one question at a time, with the recommended answer first. Each question accepts the answer unknown.
Before it asks, the skill reads the tech_stack block of onboarding.yaml and any PRD for the project. It asks only what those files leave open.
The skill writes the answers to a scaffold spec file that a JSON schema validates. It records an unknown answer as unknown and never guesses a value.
A rule table in the framework maps the spec to a topology bundle. In o1 the table holds typescript-nextjs only. Any other spec stops with a named gap.
The skill shows the pick and the spec answers that decided it. The owner confirms or overrides the pick, and the skill records the choice in the spec.
The typescript-nextjs bundle ships a starter directory with a minimal source tree, its tool configuration and exact pinned versions. The bundle VERSION gets a minor bump.
One copy script copies the starter, handbooks, CI files and topology anchor into workspace/<name>/. The generated tree passes check-secrets.sh.
Generated CI fails below the coverage floor and on a lint, typecheck or build fault. The floor is 80 percent, or the spec value when it is higher.
A typescript-nextjs fixture has one seeded fault for each gate. A framework CI test proves each gate fails on its fault and passes on the clean starter. The PR records the added CI time.
The /handover harnessability assessment rates the generated typescript-nextjs project high on all five dimensions.
The skill writes one proposed AgDR for the scaffold. The AgDR lists each stack choice and the spec answers that drove it.
/scaffold is a bootstrap skill, and its bootstrap scope names each path it writes. Hakim reviews that scope and approves it before the slice PR merges.

The skill text and each generated Markdown file pass bin/check-writing-profile.sh with zero faults. CLAUDE.md, README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/whats-inside.md and topologies/README.md list /scaffold with correct skill counts.
The rule table adds python-fastapi and go-data-pipeline. When the language answer is unknown, the skill asks about team skills and recommends a language from them.
The skill lists each spec need that no bundle covers as a gap, for example a second service shape. When no bundle fits, it offers a custom start and an upstream topology request.
The python-fastapi and go-data-pipeline bundles ship starter directories with exact pinned versions. Each bundle VERSION gets a minor bump.
Generated CI for each new bundle enforces the ac1-8 gates. Each bundle fixture installs only its own toolchain, and the PR records the added CI time.
Generated CI checks architecture layer boundaries for each topology bundle. TypeScript projects use the dependency-cruiser config from the harness golden-path initiative.
For a web shape, the interview asks for a bundle-size budget. When the spec names one, generated CI fails above it.
The generated project has one fitness-functions file that lists each gate, its threshold and the spec answer that set it.
Each new gate has a seeded fault in each bundle fixture. The framework CI test proves the gate fails on its fault and passes on the clean case.
The scaffold writes a short demo script into the project. The script lists the steps of the project's main happy path.
A scaffolded project starts locally with one command.
The project ships seed data, and every name, ID and email in it is fictional.
One command resets the project to its seed, so every demo starts from a known state.
